title: Identifying action-reaction pairs
canonical_question: How do you identify the action-reaction force pair in an interaction?
summary: Every third-law pair involves two different bodies acting on each other.
When you push a wall, you (A) push the wall (B); the wall pushes back on you with an equal force.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: Name both bodies
sections.body_md: Every third-law pair involves two different bodies acting on each other. Write the force as "A pushes B" and its partner is always "B pushes A", equal in size and opposite in direction. If both forces act on the same body, they are not a third-law pair.

sections.heading: A worked identification
sections.body_md: When you push a wall, you (A) push the wall (B); the wall pushes back on you with an equal force. The pair is you-on-wall and wall-on-you, not the wall’s push versus your weight. Matching the two bodies is the whole trick.

key_points: A pair always links two different bodies.
Swap the roles: A-on-B pairs with B-on-A.
Two forces on one body are never a pair.
core.bridge_to_parent: It puts the objective’s pairing rule into practice.

seeds: Why don’t the paired forces cancel?
